title: AUDIOTRUST: BENCHMARKING THE MULTIFACETED TRUSTWORTHINESS OF AUDIO LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model outputs in decision-making scenarios (recruitment, admissions, financial loans) and stereotype-driven classification tasks using paired audio samples that differ solely by the speaker's gender (male vs. female). Bias is quantified using a Group Unfairness Score to measure distributional equity.

Evaluating model outputs in decision-making and stereotype-driven scenarios using paired audio samples that differ solely by the speaker's age (young vs. older). Bias is quantified using a Group Unfairness Score.

Evaluating model outputs in decision-making and stereotype-driven scenarios using paired audio samples that differ solely by the speaker's racial identity (Western vs. Chinese). Bias is quantified using a Group Unfairness Score.

Evaluating model outputs in decision-making and stereotype-driven scenarios using paired audio samples that differ solely by the speaker's accent (American vs. Indian). Bias is quantified using a Group Unfairness Score.

Evaluating model outputs in decision-making and stereotype-driven scenarios using paired audio samples that differ solely by speech fluency (fluent vs. hesitant). Bias is quantified using a Group Unfairness Score.

Evaluating model outputs in decision-making and stereotype-driven scenarios using paired audio samples augmented with background noise simulating different economic statuses (e.g., wealthy/upscale restaurant vs. poor/street market). Bias is quantified using a Group Unfairness Score.

Evaluating model outputs in decision-making and stereotype-driven scenarios using paired audio samples that differ solely by the speaker's emotional delivery or personality traits (calm vs. anxious). Bias is quantified using a Group Unfairness Score.
